comparison.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a robot-gripper opening stop, then verifies its setting; PR-1766 clamps locking pliers onto a tube so they remain attached after release.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate needs two-tool coaxial adjustment and countertorque; PR-1766 needs one-gripper transport and squeeze past a spring-latch lock point while avoiding lateral drag.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires accurate angle, seated/retained nuts, three functional cycles and low drift; PR-1766 requires the pliers latched on the marked band, level, unsupported and still. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparison.reason: Although both verify locking after release, the tested mechanisms differ materially: preserving an adjustable screw setting under jam-nut torque versus crossing a handheld pliers latch threshold.
